conditions: tongue-flick (TF) counts, 60 s per trial, to a cotton swab presented 2 cm in front of the snout by one experimenter blind to treatment; swab dipped in deionised water and rolled over the cloaca of the donor, distilled water as inodorous control; each focal animal received one stimulus per day, order of presentation randomised, each swab used once; trials 1100 to 1500 h GMT; wild family groups (one adult male, one adult female, one juvenile) collected on the Chafarinas Islands in April, held in groups in indoor terraria for at least two months before testing, 15 min acclimation in the test cage; familiarity is assumed from field grouping and shared housing, not verified genetically; juveniles could not be sexed reliably; Experiment 1 tested 10 adult males and 10 adult females with water, an unfamiliar juvenile and their familiar juvenile; Experiment 2 tested 14 juveniles with water and familiar and unfamiliar adult males and females; Results sentence for males: 'In males, there were no significant differences between TF rates to the scent of the familiar or an unfamiliar juvenile (p = 0.99)'; the range of male responses to familiar juvenile scent was greater than in females and 'only 50% of males showed higher responses to the familiar juvenile.'; both sexes gave higher TF rates to every juvenile stimulus than to water (Tukey's tests, p < 0.0003 in all cases); juveniles: TF rates differed among the five treatments (repeated measures GLM, F4,52 = 24.49, p < 0.0001) and were lower to water than to any conspecific stimulus (Tukey's tests, p < 0.0006); juveniles did discriminate adult males: responses to an unfamiliar male were lower than to the familiar male (p < 0.03) and to the familiar (p = 0.0036) or unfamiliar female (p = 0.0085), while the familiar male did not differ from the familiar (p = 0.95) or unfamiliar female (p = 0.99), which did not differ from each other (p = 0.99); the Abstract states juveniles 'recognize familiar from unfamiliar males'; the authors 'lack data of the actual paternity and genetic relatedness'; null results from 10 males and 14 juveniles are low-powered
